lots.what_it_is: Box of three tiny proof gold coins plus two gold-coloured non-gold pieces. (1) Cook Islands 2012 $5 Captain James Cook, Macquarie Mint 'Smallest Gold Coin of the World', .585 gold, 0.5 g, 11 mm, in a 2x2 holder with its certificate. (2) Ned Kelly tiny gold coin in a capsule; the photo 3 obverse (Elizabeth II, Cook Islands 2012) is probably this coin's reverse side. (3) Niue 2010 $5 tiny gold coin in a capsule. (4) A larger gold-coloured coin in a cardboard flip, probably base metal. (5) A 'Tet Offensive Gold Proof Coin' (50 Years, Ba Ria Vietnam 1968, red crystal), gold-plated, boxed.
lots.guide_summary: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. Nothing verified: the WebSearch budget is used up and the coins could not be found by searching dealer sites directly. Melt floor only: the Downies live metal price (AUD, page opened 29 Sep 2026) shows gold at A$5,960.40 per troy oz, which is A$191.63 per gram. The Cook coin holds 0.5 g x .585 = 0.2925 g fine gold, about A$56 melt (read from its certificate). If the Ned Kelly and Niue coins are the same 0.5 g .585 series, which is likely but not confirmed, the three coins hold about A$168 of gold. A scrap buyer would pay about 80 to 90 percent of that. The plated medal and the flip coin are worth little.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence survived (none was offered), so both maximums are 0. For reference only, not a maximum bid: a melt floor of about A$56 per 0.5 g .585 coin, or about A$168 for three if all three are confirmed, would at a 22% premium support a hammer of at most A$168 / 1.22 = A$137 before any resale margin. Rate used: gold A$5,960.40 per oz (Downies live price, https://www.downies.com/search?q=smallest+gold+coin, page opened 29 Sep 2026).
lots.confidence_reason: The Cook coin's metal and weight were read from its certificate, but there is no SOLD, UNSOLD or ASKING evidence at all. The purity and weight of the Ned Kelly and Niue coins are unread.
lots.condition: Coins look bright and uncirculated in capsules or holders. The Cook certificate is present. The medal is boxed with its card sleeve. Nothing obvious is damaged, but the certificates for the other coins are not shown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 4 certificate: Captain James Cook, $5, .585 gold, proof, 2012, Cook Islands, 0.5 g, 11 mm, signed Chris Sealey, Macquarie Mint, 'Smallest Gold Coin of the World'. Photo 3: a Cook Islands 2012 obverse and a Niue 2010 Elizabeth II obverse in capsules. Photo 2: Captain Cook reverse in a 2x2 holder and Ned Kelly reverse in a capsule. Photo 1: box with 'Tet Offensive Gold Proof Coin' (Ba Ria, Vietnam 1968, 50 Years) plus a larger gold-coloured coin in a flip, which the researcher wrongly counted as a fourth tiny gold coin. Only three tiny gold coins are visible.
